news.headline: Nasdaq closed -0.21% and S&P -0.52%, both down for a 2nd straight week; Dow fell 654 points (-1.24%).
Oil jumped: WTI closed above $103 (+4%), Brent $116.72, highest since April, on Iran strike fears.
Iran threatened strikes on Gulf oil, data center and AI infrastructure if attacked again.
Fed meets Wednesday; markets price only ~5% odds of a hike, but ~80% for December.
10-year yield edged up to ~4.99%, staying under 5% after Thursday's big drop.
UMich sentiment at 48.0, second-lowest on record; 1-year inflation expectations rose to 4.7%.
Cybersecurity rallied 5-7% (PANW, NET) on a strong budget survey; airlines fell 4%+ on fuel costs.
Apple briefly passed Nvidia in market value (~$5.1T each) before Nvidia took the lead back.
VIX rose 3.6% to 19.72 into next week's earnings and Fed cluster.

takeaway: Tech closed only slightly lower after Thursday's AI capex rout, but oil above $103 and a weak consumer kept pressure on. Next week decides direction: FOMC Wed 2 PM plus MSFT/GOOGL that night, then GDP/PCE and AMZN Thursday.
